acceptance_criteria: A1 interaction partial R-squared at least 0.005
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared above 0 on low-volatility holdout rows
Net daily edge after the 0.10% round-trip taker cost is positive
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lag-1 BTC coefficient is larger in low-volatility regimes than in high-volatility regimes (positive interaction), and lag-1 BTC explains a positive out-of-sample component of next-bar target returns within low-volatility rows.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-bar target return predicted from its own lagged return, the common factor and lag-1 BTC, with the interaction excluded
cost_assumptions: OKX VIP0 taker fee 0.05% per side, from the OKX public fee schedule (okx.com/fees), checked 2026-11-18; treated as an assumption, not verified for the user's account
Funding rate costs ignored; perpetual funding can exceed taker fees over holding periods
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
spec.cost_model: Round-trip taker cost 0.10% per position flip (OKX VIP0 taker 0.05% per side, assumed); sign rule on out-of-sample augmented forecasts on low-volatility holdout rows only, 1x, flat on high-volatility rows; entry from flat and final exit cost one taker side each; funding, slippage and market impact ignored
exclusions: Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the panel
Hyperliquid candles that are unclosed or carry zero trades are excluded
Rows without a regime label are excluded and counted (the first 281 daily return rows and the first 749 hourly return rows, given study 001's panel sizes)
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18T16:00Z are out of sample
known_confounders: The 30-day volatility window and median-split regime rule mirror study 001's post-hoc descriptive split; the fresh dimensions are the pair (BTC→SOL) and the frequency (1H), not the regime definition
The third-asset common-factor proxy is itself driven by BTC and may absorb part of the transmission effect; no-factor controls are reported as upper bounds
Common crypto market shocks move BTC, ETH and SOL together; the regressions control for the contemporaneous third-asset return only
Hyperliquid same-period prices are highly correlated with OKX prices, so the cross-venue check cannot serve as independent evidence
Daily bars are anchored at 16:00 UTC (OKX) and 00:00 UTC (Hyperliquid); the lag-1 effect is defined on each venue's own grid
spec.mechanism: In low-volatility regimes, orderly price discovery lets information repriced in the largest, most liquid market (BTC perpetuals) transmit to smaller markets with a lag, while in high-volatility regimes simultaneous repricing and liquidation-driven flows erase the lag. Study 001 found no unconditional lag-1 transmission; its post-hoc descriptive split suggested the effect may be concentrated in low-volatility regimes.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count; rows without a regime label (warm-up) are excluded and counted
model_definition: Interaction OLS with HAC standard errors (daily BTC→SOL, 1H BTC→ETH)
Low-volatility-subsample partial lead-lag with HAC standard errors
Regime-aware purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation (low-volatility holdout rows only)
Hyperliquid daily BTC→ETH low-volatility subsample as a descriptive cross-venue check (not in the test family)
spec.multiple_testing_family: Regime-conditional BTC transmission, daily BTC→SOL and 1H BTC→ETH (4 tests: A1 daily interaction, A2 daily low-volatility subsample, B1 1H interaction, B2 1H low-volatility subsample)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lag-1 BTC returns have no regime-dependent incremental predictive value: the interaction coefficient is zero and lag-1 BTC does not predict target returns within low-volatility rows, beyond the target's own history and the common-factor control, after costs and dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the BTC×lowvol interaction in the daily BTC→SOL interaction regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted A1 interaction p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0 on low-volatility holdout rows
Net daily edge after costs is zero or negative
spec.research_question: Does lag-1 BTC perpetual return predict the next-bar target perpetual return more strongly in low-volatility regimes than in high-volatility regimes, on a fresh pair (daily BTC→SOL) and a fresh frequency (1H BTC→ETH)?
spec.target_definition: Next-day close-to-close SOL-USDT perpetual log return (daily primary); next-hour ETH-USDT perpetual log return (1H secondary)
spec.title: Low-volatility regimes strengthen BTC transmission
